semantic_review.finding: Same mandatory lowercase name, optional lowercase export alias and conditional default key. Entry allocation, tombstoned slots, remove_files, lookup APIs and other indices are byte-identical outside the sole export registration replacement. Existing symbol numbering, removal/re-add semantics and candidate identities remain; no global cache or lifetime extension was introduced.

Lazy split/zip computes the same maximal common prefix over original strip_ext output, including empty path segments, separators, case-sensitive unknown extensions and Unicode. Only intermediate Vec<&str> allocations are removed.

Every candidate is still scanned. The monotonically increasing best-distance tracker retains every tie for the final maximum in original input order, then calls unchanged stable_candidates. Original sorting, adjacent identity deduplication, uniqueness decision, confidence and candidate_count_penalty remain. Empty input still yields empty/None. No candidate early-drop rule, best-of execution or shortened external file scan was added.

Complete fixed-base comparison contains no other production file. External-edit detection, dependency closure, root pending, epoch/CAS, fallback, transaction/drop and workload/acceptance budgets are not edited. Resolver outputs remain the semantic input to those unchanged mechanisms.

Explicit repeated work is removed, but no timing/RSS improvement is measured. One-pass best.clear() keeps allocated capacity: many earlier low-distance ties followed by one better candidate can retain a larger temporary index buffer than the old final-ties-only collection. Worst-case remainsO(C); do not claim allocation/peakRSS improves for every input or that this fixes the prior100k failures.
